title: Why csm-plan/csm-build Sessions Stop With Work Remaining

tldr.content: Stopping is caused by a few instruction/harness defects, not model limits. Ranked: (1) acceptance signals may be disjunctive ('Either ... OR record a deferral') and csm-build's Completion Gate reads task STATUS, so tasks are marked completed with the feature unbuilt; (2) the canonical JSON plans and build-state records are ungated, and the build-state cursor is inconsistent with the SKILL, so the durable record is abandoned; (3) the 'do not stop' rule is prose-only with no deterministic completion gate; (4) the tmux bootstrap can end the invocation before work runs; (5) successor-plan proliferation is enabled by the missing typed supersession field. Fix = make these deterministic (Stop-gate, single positive acceptance signals, supersession field, mandatory gated plan close).

executiveSummary.content:
Question: why do csm-plan/csm-build sessions stop with work remaining? Four tracks (csm-build SKILL/lib, csm-plan SKILL/schema, artifact corpus, external practice) were synthesized, challenged, and judged (v1 failed the judge on factual/citation accuracy and was remediated).

```text
Question -> Triage (DEEP x hybrid)
  -> R1 csm-build -> R2 csm-plan -> R3 corpus (60 plans) -> R4 external
  -> Synthesis -> Challenge -> Judge (fail) -> Remediate -> Verified finding
```

Headline: the completion doctrine (checkpoint != complete; runnable acceptance signals; resumable cursor) is sound and in places exceeds external practice, but enforcement is prose-only and the plan schema accepts signals the SKILL forbids. Corpus: 60 plans (30 complete/16 in_progress/9 ready/5 blocked), 429 tasks, 198 pending / 230 open; 21 plans for one goal.

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported — acceptance-signal validation gap + status-only Completion Gate let completed tasks carry unbuilt deliverables [ref-plan-skill][ref-plan-schema][ref-plan-finalwork][ref-plan-remainder].
K2. supported — canonical JSON plans are ungated; the plan-corpus check filters *-csm.md [ref-check-suite].
K3. partially-supported — build-state cursor pins nextTransition to the first transition, inconsistent with the SKILL; CHECKPOINT->COMPLETE is legal/tested [ref-build-state][ref-build-tests].
K4. supported — 'do not stop' is prose-only; no deterministic completion gate [ref-build-skill][ref-check-suite].
K5. partially-supported — tmux bootstrap can end the invocation pre-execution (design intent is a detached runner) [ref-build-skill].
K6. partially-supported — supersession only lacks a typed schema field; resolvable out-of-band; 21 DWRR plans [ref-plan-schema][ref-readme].
K7. supported — the durable record is left unclosed (9 complete-with-open-tasks; 9/23 build-state non-terminal) [ref-plan-lib][ref-build-state].
K8. supported — input-gate contradiction (five required vs DDD/norms optional) and current-context bypassing the Completion Gate [ref-build-state][ref-build-ctx].
K9. supported — external practice separates the stop decision from the worker (Stop hook / evaluator) and adds run-level ceilings; CSM lacks both [ref-cc-best][ref-cc-hooks][ref-cc-goal].

detailSections.content:
D1 Acceptance-signal escape: the SKILL mandates one positive signal but the schema permits any non-empty string, so 5 DWRR task rows marked completed took the 'OR record a deferral' branch [ref-plan-skill][ref-plan-schema][ref-plan-finalwork][ref-plan-remainder].

D2 Ungated canonical record: check-suite validates only *-csm.md; 60 JSON plans and 23 build-state files are unchecked; the build-state validator pins nextTransition to the first transition (cursor mismatch, not a rejected transition) [ref-check-suite][ref-build-state][ref-build-tests].

D3 Stop authorities: tmux bootstrap step 4; 'incomplete' output status; REPAIR two-attempt stop; BLOCKED rules; orchestrate maxAttempts default 2 [ref-build-skill][ref-build-out][ref-co-recovery].

D4 Input-gate contradiction: lib requires all five inputs; SKILL labels DDD/norms optional; current-context auto-walks to COMPLETE without the Completion Gate [ref-build-state][ref-build-skill][ref-build-ctx].

D5 Proliferation: no typed supersession field; 21 DWRR plans; supersession tracked in README prose [ref-plan-schema][ref-readme].

D6 Corpus: 60 plans/429 tasks/198 pending/230 open; build-state 9/23 non-terminal (BLOCKED terminal); 9 complete-with-open-tasks; recurring journal text uncommitted (22), deferred (9), superseded (10) [ref-plan-lib][ref-build-state].

D7 External: deterministic Stop hook blocks turn end until a script passes; TaskCompleted blocks completion; /goal uses a separate evaluator; run-level no-progress/budget ceilings. CSM has the doctrine, not the enforcement [ref-cc-best][ref-cc-hooks][ref-cc-goal].

recommendation.content:
Recommend: treat this as an instruction/harness defect set and fix it deterministically; the doctrine is sound. Confidence: high on causes; medium on fix efficacy until trialed.

Prioritized fixes:
1. Require each acceptanceSignal to be one positive runnable command that fails until the deliverable exists; forbid 'Either ... OR defer' (add a lint); make genuine deferrals their own blocked task with the user decision required [K1].
2. Extend check-suite's plan gate to the canonical *-csm.json plans and the csm-build-state records; fail on pending/in_progress without a recorded blocker [K2][K7].
3. Add a first-class typed supersession field to the plan schema and require creation to close the predecessor [K6].
4. Add a deterministic stop gate (Stop-hook analogue) so the COMPLETE vs continue decision is not self-judged; add run-level no-progress/budget ceilings [K9].
5. Reconcile the build-state cursor: accept/derive the declared next transition and require the record be written via the lib [K3].
6. Make tmux bootstrap conditional, and never end an invocation with a non-terminal Control unless PAUSED/BLOCKED was written [K5].
7. Fix the input-gate contradiction and run the Completion Gate inside the current-context path [K8].
8. Add a commit-ledger field and reconcile obligations at CHECKPOINT [claim-commit-stale][claim-obligations].

What would change the answer: a controlled trial showing the fixes do not reduce stops per run. Cost of being wrong: continued re-planning churn (21 plans for one goal) and features closed as 'completed' while unbuilt.

unverifiedClaims.content: U1. Whether the fixes empirically reduce premature stops needs a controlled trial. U2. The proportion of the 198 pending tasks genuinely unbuilt vs re-homed into successors is unresolved (no per-task git ownership mapping). U3. Some complete plans carry open tasks by legitimate reconciliation against successors; the corpus cannot always distinguish that from an unclosed record.

processAppendix.content: Tier DEEP x hybrid. Tracks R1-R4. Synthesized primary-led; independent challenger (downgraded claim-state-validator to a cursor defect, corrected record-unclosed counts to 9/23 non-terminal, recast deferral-signals as a validation gap, softened proliferation, added the ungated-JSON claim) and judge (v1 FAIL factual 0.40 / citation 0.60; remediated to v2). VERIFY primary-personal.

claims.statement: csm-build's Tmux Session Bootstrap is the mandated first step and step 4 says to end the invocation when a detached session was launched; on a host without an already-active tmux session the normal case hits this and the current invocation ends before execution — although the intent is that the detached session runs the build.

citations.quote: If a new detached session was launched, end the invocation — tmux does the build from the start.

claims.statement: The canonical build-state cursor is inconsistent with the SKILL: the validator pins control.nextTransition to the FIRST transition of the current state, so a record parked at CHECKPOINT must declare 'CHECKPOINT -> SELECT' even though the SKILL tells the agent to choose SELECT/COMPLETE/BLOCKED and record the exact next transition. CHECKPOINT->COMPLETE itself is legal and tested (state.mjs:38; build-json-control.test.mjs), so the defect is a cursor-vocabulary mismatch, not a rejected transition.

citations.quote: next transition does not match the lifecycle state
walks CHECKPOINT -> COMPLETE and asserts validity
From CHECKPOINT, transition to SELECT, COMPLETE, or BLOCKED

claims.statement: The 'do not stop after one task or cycle' rule is prose-only: no gate enforces continuation or task completion, and the plan-corpus gate in check-suite only covers '*-csm.md' projections, so the canonical 'csm-plan/1' JSON corpus (60 files) is not validated by CI.

citations.quote: Do not stop after one task or cycle

claims.statement: csm-build's executable input gate requires all five inputs (plan/bdd/tests/ddd/norms) unconditionally, while the SKILL labels only DDD/norms optional (NORMS.md 'entirely optional') and treats plan/bdd/tests as required; and the current-context executor auto-walks INTEGRATE->CHECKPOINT->COMPLETE via completeBuild without evaluating Completion Gate conditions 1-8.

The strongest single cause is a validation/enforcement gap: csm-plan's SKILL mandates exactly one positive runnable acceptance signal (SKILL.md:358), but the schema only requires a non-empty string (csm-plan.schema.json:109) and no lint rejects disjunctive 'Either ... OR record/document/keep a deferral' signals; csm-build Completion Gate #1 then reads task STATUS, so tasks are marked completed with the feature unbuilt (observed in 5 tasks across the two 2026-09-14 DWRR plans).

citations.quote: the one runnable command/test whose pass objectively proves this task done
Either ... OR the opt-in decision is explicitly recorded
OR the scope decision ... is explicitly recorded
Every numbered task is completed or explicitly excluded

claims.statement: Successor-plan proliferation is enabled by the absence of a typed in-artifact supersession field: csm-plan.schema.json is additionalProperties:false with no supersedes/supersededBy property, while csm-build looks for a 'typed supersession pointer' in the descriptor. Supersession is nonetheless resolvable out-of-band via .agents/README.md prose and 'closed as superseded' nextTransition strings; the dynamic-worker-runtime goal spans 21 plans (12 frozen siblings).

citations.quote: Check the selected JSON descriptor for its typed supersession pointer

claims.statement: The corpus shows records left unclosed: 9 plans marked complete still carry open tasks; 3 non-complete plans carry no status:'pending' tasks (though they hold in_progress/blocked tasks, so they are not simply 'done-but-unclosed'); and build-state records are 9/23 non-terminal (BLOCKED is terminal, so 14/23 terminal). Aggregate: 60 plans, 429 tasks, 198 pending, 230 open.

Commit policy is a static string ('commits: disabled') with no commit-ledger field in the plan schema; 34/60 plans are 'disabled' (9/14 recent completes) even though the work was committed by successors, so the record cannot distinguish uncommitted work and stalls at CHECKPOINT.

csm-plan's planning terminal (SAVED) is not the artifact's terminal: plans are born ready/NOT_STARTED and only a later human message starts them, with no owner/trigger; 9 plans are ready/NOT_STARTED carrying 57 status:'pending' tasks.

Applicability obligations form a mostly unclosed second gate: across 54 applicability records (52 warranted), 51 keep every obligation 'required' and only 1 carries 'satisfied' obligations; neither skill instructs an obligation-status update at CHECKPOINT, and Completion Gate #1 does not consult obligations.

Legal low-evidence stop forks exist: 'incomplete' is an accepted executor status with no repair path; REPAIR stops after two attempts; broad BLOCKED rules; and the orchestrate handoff retries at most maxAttempts (default 2, csm-orchestrate/lib/recovery.mjs).

citations.quote: After two failed attempts ... stop patching

claims.statement: External practice separates the stop decision from the worker: a deterministic Stop hook runs a check as a script and blocks the turn from ending until it passes (8-block override), and TaskCompleted can prevent a task being marked complete; /goal uses a separate evaluator model that sends the agent back to work. csm-build has none of these — the stop decision is self-judged at CHECKPOINT and enforcement is prose-only; it also has no run-level no-progress/budget ceiling.

citations.quote: a Stop hook runs your check as a script and blocks the turn from ending until it passes
a small fast model checks whether the condition holds ... starts another turn

claims.statement: The canonical csm-plan/1 JSON plans are ungated: check-suite's plan-corpus loop filters files ending '-csm.md', so the authoritative JSON plans (60 files) escape Control/journal/task validation in CI — drift in the durable record is invisible.

Whether fixing these instruction-level issues actually makes a csm-build run continue to completion is not yet demonstrated; it requires a controlled trial (apply the fixes, run a plan to COMPLETE, measure stops per run).
